content.p: This Act may be cited as the Customs Amendment (Miscellaneous Measures) Act 2013.

Each provision of this Act specified in column 1 of the table commences, or is taken to have commenced, in accordance with column 2 of the table. Any other statement in column 2 has effect according to its terms.

section.heading: Offence for bringing restricted goods into Australia

content.p: A person commits an offence of strict liability if:
the person brings goods into Australia; and
the goods are restricted goods.
Penalty: 1,000 penalty units.
Note: For strict liability, see section 6.1 of the Criminal Code.
Subsection (1) does not apply if the person brings the goods into Australia in accordance with a written permission given by the Minister for the purposes of this subsection.
(3) For the purposes of this Act, restricted goods are goods:
that, if imported, would be prohibited imports; and
that are prescribed by the regulations for the purposes of this definition.
This section has effect only for purposes related to external affairs, including:
for purposes related to giving effect to an international agreement to which Australia is a party; and
for purposes related to addressing matters of international concern.

hcontainer.name: part
hcontainer.heading: Entry of ships or aircraft for home consumption or warehousing

content.p: After “goods to which section 68 applies that are unshipped”, insert “or that are a ship or aircraft not carried on board a ship or aircraft”.
Omit “unshipped”, substitute “goods to which paragraph (a) of this subsection applies”.
Repeal the subsections, substitute:
The owner of goods to which this section applies may enter the goods for home consumption or for warehousing:
for goods carried on board a ship or aircraft—at any time before the ship or aircraft first arrives at a port or airport in Australia at which any goods are to be discharged; or
for goods that are a ship or aircraft and that are not carried on board a ship or aircraft—at any time before the ship or aircraft first arrives at a port or airport in Australia.

If the owner of goods to which this section applies does not enter the goods under subsection (2) for home consumption or for warehousing, the owner must enter the goods for home consumption or for warehousing:
for goods carried on board a ship or aircraft—after the ship or aircraft first arrives at a port or airport in Australia at which any goods are to be discharged; or
for goods that are a ship or aircraft and that are not carried on board a ship or aircraft—after the ship or aircraft first arrives at a port or airport in Australia.
Repeal the subsections, substitute:
If:
an import declaration is, or is taken under section 71L to have been, communicated to Customs; and
before the time when the declaration is, or is so taken to have been, communicated to Customs, the goods to which the declaration relates:
have been imported; or
for goods carried on board a ship or aircraft—have been brought to the first port or airport in Australia at which any goods are to be discharged; or
for goods that are a ship or aircraft and that are not carried on board a ship or aircraft—have arrived at a port or airport in Australia;
the goods are taken to have been entered for home consumption.
If:
an import declaration is, or is taken under section 71L to have been, communicated to Customs; and
at the time when the declaration is, or is so taken to have been, communicated to Customs, the goods to which the declaration relates:
for goods carried on board a ship or aircraft—have not been brought to the first port or airport in Australia at which any goods are to be discharged; or
for goods that are a ship or aircraft and that are not carried on board a ship or aircraft—have not arrived at a port or airport in Australia;

the goods are taken to be entered for home consumption only when they are brought to that first port or airport in Australia or when they arrive at a port or airport in Australia (as the case requires).
Repeal the subsection, substitute:
If:
the goods are goods to which section 68 applies; and
the goods have not been entered for home consumption or warehousing; and
subsection (2C) does not apply to the goods;
a movement application may be made only by:

for goods carried on board a ship or aircraft—the operator of the ship or aircraft, a cargo reporter in relation to the goods, or a stevedore or depot operator who has, or intends to take, possession of the goods; or
for goods that are a ship or aircraft and that are not carried on board a ship or aircraft—the owner of the goods.
Repeal the heading, substitute:

content.p: Omit “either be entered for warehousing under paragraph 68(2)(b) or for transhipment under paragraph 68(2)(c)”, substitute “be entered for warehousing under subsection 68(2) or (3)”.
The amendment made by item 12 does not affect the validity of entries of goods for home consumption or warehousing made before the commencement of that item.
The amendment made by item 14 does not affect the validity of movement applications made before the commencement of that item.

section.heading: CEO may require applicant to supply further information

content.p: The CEO may, by written notice given to an applicant for a warehouse licence, require the applicant to supply further information in relation to the application within the period that is specified in the notice.
The CEO may extend the specified period if the applicant, in writing, requests the CEO to do so.
If the applicant:
fails to supply the further information within the specified period, or that period as extended under subsection (2); but
supplies the information at a later time;
the CEO must not take the information into account in determining whether to grant the warehouse licence.
Omit “made in”, substitute “made under section 80 or 80A in relation to”.
Repeal the subsection, substitute:
If an application for a warehouse licence is made, the CEO must decide whether or not to grant the licence within 60 days after:
if paragraph (b) does not apply—the receipt of the application; or

if the CEO, under section 80A, requires the applicant to supply further information in relation to the application and the applicant supplies the information in accordance with that section—the receipt of the information.
The amendments made by this Part apply in relation to applications for warehouse licences made on or after the commencement of this Part.

hcontainer.name: part
hcontainer.heading: Notification of particulars of cargo reporters

content.p: Add:

A cargo reporter who is required to make a report under this section is not liable to be prosecuted for, and cannot be served with an infringement notice under Division 5 of Part XIII for, an offence against this section if:
the cargo reporter made a report, but contravened subsection (4) of this section; and

(b) the time (the actual time of arrival) at which the ship or aircraft in question arrived at the first port or airport in Australia since it last departed from a port or airport outside Australia was later than the estimated time of arrival referred to in subsection 64AB(8); and
the cargo reporter would not have contravened subsection (4) of this section if the estimated time of arrival of the ship or aircraft had been its actual time of arrival.
